key_insight: The paper presents an interpretable, scalable method for large hierarchical probabilistic time‑series forecasting that provides both temporal attributions and uncertainty explanations across aggregation levels, enabling transparent demand predictions for industry.
problem_solved: Opaque ML models for hierarchical demand forecasting make it hard to trace drivers of predictions across levels and over time, and to explain predictive uncertainty; this work closes that interpretability gap while keeping performance and scalability for industrial hierarchies.
method: Adapt generic interpretability techniques to hierarchical structures so attributions can be allocated consistently across aggregation levels (top→bottom and bottom→top).
Generate temporal explanations (time‑local attributions) and uncertainty decompositions for probabilistic forecasts (e.g., explain shifts in quantiles or predictive variance).
Design scalable algorithms (aggregation‑aware attribution, efficient sampling/approximation) to handle large industrial hierarchies and high-volume time series.
impact: Provides practitioners with actionable, trustworthy explanations for forecast drivers and uncertainty, improving debugging, inventory/planning decisions, and stakeholder trust in automated forecasting systems.
visual_elements: Hierarchical tree diagram with colored contribution heatmap showing how forecast drivers distribute across levels (SKU → category → region).
Time series plot with stacked/overlaid attribution ribbons plus predictive uncertainty bands to show when and why forecasts change.
Bar or waterfall chart comparing aggregate vs. disaggregated contributions to highlight reconciliation and root causes.
Pipeline flowchart: model → probabilistic forecast → attribution module → temporal & uncertainty explanation outputs (scalable components highlighted).
paper_title: Hierarchical Industrial Demand Forecasting with Temporal and Uncertainty Explanations
paper_authors: Harshavardhan Kamarthi, Shangqing Xu, Xinjie Tong, Xingyu Zhou, James Peters
